$comment: Descriptors this repository ships that `frictionless` refuses, and why each is still here. Read scripts/check_frictionless.py before editing: an entry closes nothing. The refusal goes on being reported and this check goes on failing until the entry is deleted, and it can be deleted only by the refusal being gone. It reddens when the refusal changes, when the declaration moves, and when the fix lands, so it cannot go stale in silence. A refusal with no entry here fails too. `frictionless_version` is held to the version installed when the check runs, because a refusal measured against one implementation and read against another reads exactly like one measured now.

notes: constraint "pattern" is not supported by type "number"
rejections.blocked_on: A regeneration of this descriptor against finetype b2ba501a or later, and then a republish of the object. The engine that wrote this field routed every constraint the label's validation states into `constraints` without reference to the declared type; it now routes each keyword by the declared type's Data Package v2 vocabulary and carries what the type has no place for on `x-finetype-unsupported-constraints`. Re-emitting is what moves these keywords. Editing them here would not: `scripts/stamp_descriptor.py` writes the descriptor into the object's own Parquet footer and the descriptor declares that object's sha256, so this repository's copy cannot move ahead of the object's without `check_descriptors.py` reporting the two as different.
rejections.reason: `confidence` is declared `number` and carries the digit-shape `pattern` that finetype's label validation states. v2's `number` branch gives `constraints` `minimum`/`maximum`/`enum`/`required`/`unique` and no `pattern`, so the whole package is refused for it. The pattern is true of the column; the standard has nowhere to put it on this type.

All three are true of the column and none has a place on this type.
